predecessors.name: Mongol Empire
predecessors.text: the Chagatai ulus within the Mongol Empire: 'the regions roughly corresponding to the defunct Qara Khitai Empire' (Issyk-Kul, the Ili, Chu and Talas rivers, Transoxania, the Tarim Basin)

successors.name: Moghulistan
successors.text: the Moghul khanate after Esen Buqa II's death: 'in the west Yunus Khan gained power, while in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan'

ledger.x: 1294: the Chagatai Khanate stands among the successors of the Mongol Empire, ruled by Duwa.
1306: Chapar surrenders to Duwa and the Ögedeid ulus of Kaidu ends.
1346: Qazaghan kills Qazan Khan and the khanate splits in two.
1347: the Dughlats raise Tughlugh Timur and the eastern khanate becomes Moghulistan.
1361: the second invasion ends the contest.
1361: Transoxiana is Moghul under Ilyas Khoja.
1363: the western Tarim joins the shape.
1390: Timur beats Qamar-ud-din and Khizr Khoja takes the throne.
1395: the western and northern fringe goes to Timur.
1452: the Moghul attacks on the Syr Darya end without gain.
1462: Esen Buqa II dies and Moghulistan divides.

wars.name: Kaidu and Duwa against the Yuan
wars.outcome: Duwa attacked the Yuan garrisons in the winter of 1298 and was 'wounded and defeated' in 1301; Kaidu died in 1301; Duwa and Chapar recognised Yuan authority in 1303 and a general peace followed 'around 1304'.

wars.name: Chagatai invasions of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: Duwa 'invaded Khurasan and Mazandaran' in early 1295 while the Ilkhanid commanders were in a succession struggle; in 1315 Esen Buqa 'invaded the Ilkhanate in support of Duwa's grandson, Dawud Khoja'.

wars.name: Chagatai raids on the Delhi Sultanate
wars.outcome: Duwa invaded the Punjab in 1297 and was defeated; Prince Turghai looted the Delhi region in 1303; Kebek looted the Multan region in 1305.

wars.name: Qazaghan's rebellion
wars.outcome: Qazaghan rebelled in 1345, was defeated, and killed Qazan Khan the next year; the khanate split into a western amirate with puppet khans and the eastern Moghulistan.

wars.name: Tughlugh Timur's conquest of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Tughlugh Timur invaded in March 1360 and again in 1361 and left Ilyas Khoja as viceroy; Amir Husayn and Timur wrested the land back after Tughlugh's death in 1363.

wars.name: Timur's wars against Moghulistan
wars.outcome: Timur looted the Ili region in 1375, 'sent at least five victorious expeditions to Moghulistan' (undated) and defeated Qamar-ud-din in 1390; Khizr Khoja then ruled as Timur's son-in-law (his daughter married Timur in 1397).

wars.name: Moghul-Oirat wars
wars.outcome: Uwais Khan fought the Oirats 'sixty-one engagements ... only once was he victorious', was twice captured and lost Beshbalik and Kumul; he made Turfan his base and moved to Ilibalik.

wars.name: Moghul-Timurid wars under Esen Buqa II
wars.outcome: The Timurids took Kashgar after Uwais died and Esen Buqa retook it in 1435; in 1451 he attacked Tashkent and temporarily held Andijan.

certainty.note: Steppe, oasis and mountain frontiers throughout; no treaty or survey line is on any page opened.
